newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds follow gilts lower, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds follow gilts lower, trade thin.

text.p: Irish bonds were marked down slightly in quiet trade on Monday in line with UK gilts which have been hit by profit-taking and concerns over higher interest rates, dealers said.
"The curve has shifted up and flattened out at the short end and fears in the UK that the economy is growing too fast would seem to be impacting on the Irish market today," one dealer said.
By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down seven pence at 102.05 to yield 5.93 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down five pence at 109.80 to yield 6.54 percent.
Yields against German Bunds widened slightly from Friday's close to 156 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 90 over in the 10-year.

Gilts and short sterling took a battering on Monday, following speculation in weekend newspapers that the Bank of England would tighten interest rates by more than financial markets had been expecting.
It may well be a turbulent week for gilts ahead of Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget on July 2, with little significant economic data in the meantime to give direction.
The only UK economic data this week are trade figures on Wednesday and final first quarter GDP figures on Friday, neither of which are expected to offer much inspiration.

Financial market turbulence is not likely to end with the July 2 budget as the Bank of England's monetary policy committee meets a week later on July 9 and 10. Many economists forecast that a rate rise will follow the meeting.
Looking ahead, U.S. consumer confidence data tomorrow would be of interest, dealers said.
The domestic market will also be paying attention to the new Fianna Fail-Progressive Democratic government, which is due to be formed on Thursday.
The market wasn't expecting any surprises from the new finance minister, dealers said.
